The competition challenges participants to conceptualize, design, and develop a playable digital game within 24 hours based on a surprise theme revealed at the beginning of the event. Eligibility & Team Formation The competition is open to college students interested in game development, programming, game design, art, and related fields. Participants may register individually or in teams of up to 4 members . Students from different colleges may form a team ( inter-college teams are allowed ). Students from different specializations, branches, or academic disciplines may form a team ( inter-specialization teams are allowed ). All team members must complete the required registration process before the deadline. Competition Format Event: 24-hour digital game jam. Dates: 21–22 October 2026. Development duration: 24 hours, within the official start and submission times announced by the organizers. Theme: A surprise theme will be revealed at the beginning of the competition. Problem statements: One common theme will be announced for all participating teams. Teams must interpret the theme creatively and incorporate it meaningfully into their games. Final submission: Each team must submit a playable digital game along with the required details before the deadline. Tools & Resources Participants may use suitable game engines, programming languages, and development tools. Third-party assets, libraries, and AI tools may be used where permitted, but externally sourced assets and resources must be appropriately credited. The core game concept, gameplay, and implementation must be developed during the competition. Teams are responsible for ensuring that their games and assets comply with applicable licenses and usage permissions. Competition Rules Team Size: Each team may consist of a maximum of 4 members. Time Limit: All games must be developed and submitted within the official 24-hour competition window. Originality: Pre-existing completed games or projects may not be submitted as original jam entries. The game must be created during the competition. Playable Submission: Teams must submit a playable digital build and all information requested by the organizers before the deadline. Fair Play: Plagiarism, copying another team's work, or misrepresenting work as original may result in disqualification. Team Participation: Team members should contribute to the development process and comply with event instructions. Evaluation: Submissions may be evaluated on creativity, gameplay, theme integration, technical execution, and overall presentation. Organizer Authority: Participants must follow the official event guidelines. The organizers reserve the right to address rule violations and resolve competition-related disputes. WhatsApp Community: Participants are encouraged to join the official GameForge ’26 WhatsApp Community for important announcements, event updates, instructions, and competition-related information.
